newsitem.title: UK: Babcock in talks on sale of process div.
newsitem.headline: Babcock in talks on sale of process div.

text.p: British engineering group Babcock International Group Plc said on Tuesday it was looking to sell its process division and its U.S. Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) dust recycling plant.

Babcock said it was in active discussions with a number of interested parties on the sale of the process division and is going to start the closure of the prototype EAF dust recyling plant in Caldwell, U.S. in order to stop operating losses from the business.

It said in a statement accompanying annual results that construction activities in Africa were being scaled down to reduce risks in the business and noted that strategic options for the division are being kept under review.
The group made a pre-tax loss of 22.0 million stg in the year to March 31, 1997 after exceptional charges compared with a profit of 3.1 million last time.
The charges relates to the exceptional write-off and termination of the Caldwell plant of 27.3 million stg. Other exceptionals amounted to a gain of 1.7 million stg.

Chairman John Parker said, "Strategies are in place to deal with the underperforming business. We are confident that the core business of the group are now in a position to deliver improving profits."
Over 80 percent of Babcock's turnover is derived from its two core divisions -- materials handling and facilities management.
Babcock said the performance of the remaining businesses had "seriously undermined the group's profitability".
